subject: 🏃 Tuesday — 4 mi Easy (Wk 3)
html:
Tomorrow: 4 miles easy at 9:15–9:30 pace. This is your post-B2B recovery run — the plan intentionally drops Tuesday's track session this week, and for good reason. You raced 9.3 hilly miles with 39+ minutes in Z4/Z5 on Sunday; 48 hours later, the job is blood flow, not stimulus.

Knee is back to 1/5. The doubled mobility flush worked — Sunday's 2/5 medial PFJ tingle resolved within 24 hours. That's exactly the response we wanted. Do the standard 5-min pre-run activation before you head out: quadruped hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges, plus the PT-prescribed quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side). Quick knee check before the first step — if you feel any medial awareness during the activation, text me before running.

Execution: HR anchor ≤145 BPM, truly conversational. If you drift above 145, you're running too hard for a recovery day. Accept whatever pace that HR produces — it'll probably land around 9:15–9:30 on your flat routes, maybe slower on hills, and that's perfect.

Focus cue: Quiet feet, short stride, relaxed shoulders. The B2B showed real fast-finish capacity and your fitness is tracking ahead of schedule — resist any urge to "test" anything tomorrow. Bank the recovery.

Context: Week 3 of 12, Phase 1 Foundation & Durability — 68 days to race day. Wednesday is full-Rx heavy strength at Cañada (squat 155, RDL 155 with straps, calf raise 40/hand, reverse Nordics), so fresh legs tomorrow means better quality under the bar. The May 30 PAL 10K is 11 days out.

Tonight: Hydrate, get to bed by 10, lay out your gear and the Polar H10 strap before you turn in. Confirm the strap is charged — tomorrow's easy-run HR data is low-stakes, but building the habit of strapping on the H10 every time matters for when it counts.
